newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Steel plans 130 bln yen investment in 98/99.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Steel plans 130 bln yen investment in 98/99.

text.p: Japan's Nippon Steel Corp said on Monday it expected to spend about 130 billion yen on capital investment in the 1998/99 financial year, ending in March 1999.
This includes planned spending to build electric power plants, Tetsuo Seki, the company's managing director, told reporters.

The company plans to spend a total of 80 billion yen over the three years to March 2001 to build several electric power plants in Japan, from which it plans to sell electricity to domestic electric utilities, Seki said.
Earlier on Monday, the giant steel maker announced that it plans 95 billion yen in capital investment in 1997/98, the company's lowest-ever annual capital investment.
The previous record low was in 1996/97, when it spent 100 billion yen, the company said.

Of the 95 billion yen in spending planned for 1997/98, 65 percent will be used for cost cutting and energy conservation, while 20 percent will be used to repair and overhaul existing facilities, Seki said.
He said the company carried out no fresh spending to boost steel output capacity in 1996/97 and has no plans for such investment in 1997/98.
In the three years to March 2000 the company plans a total of 300 billion yen in capital spending, excluding the cost of building power plants, he added.
